oneOf.description: ITU‑T G.711 A‑law: 8 kHz, 8‑bit logarithmic PCM companding at 64 kbit/s; widely used in telephony outside North America/Japan.
ITU‑T G.711 μ‑law: 8 kHz, 8‑bit logarithmic PCM companding at 64 kbit/s; commonly used in North America and Japan.
MPEG‑1/2 Layer III perceptual audio codec; frequently used to distribute speech at low to medium bitrates.
Advanced Audio Coding (MPEG‑4/2 AAC); higher efficiency than MP3 for speech and general audio at comparable bitrates.
ITU‑T wideband speech codec (16 kHz sampling, 64/56/48 kbit/s) used for HD‑Voice in telephony.
ITU‑T low‑bitrate VoIP codec (5.3/6.3 kbit/s) based on CELP/MP‑MLQ, narrowband 8 kHz sampling.
ITU‑T ADPCM speech codec (16/24/32/40 kbit/s) used in legacy telephony and embedded systems.
ITU‑T CS‑ACELP narrowband speech codec at 8 kbit/s; widely deployed in VoIP; Annex B adds VAD/CNG.
GSM Full‑Rate narrowband codec (~13 kb/s) used in early GSM networks.
GSM Enhanced Full‑Rate (12.2 kb/s) improved speech quality over GSM‑FR in 2G networks.
GSM Half‑Rate (~5.6 kb/s) for increased capacity with lower bitrates.
Adaptive Multi‑Rate (NB) 3GPP codec (4.75–12.2 kb/s, 8 kHz) for mobile voice with mode adaptation and VAD/CNG.
Adaptive Multi‑Rate Wideband (G.722.2) 3GPP/ITU codec (6.6–23.85 kb/s, 16 kHz) for HD‑voice in 3G/4G.
Internet Low Bitrate Codec (13.33/15.2 kb/s, 8 kHz) robust to packet loss in VoIP.
Open‑source CELP speech codec (NB/WB modes) designed for VoIP; supports VAD/DTX/PLC.
IETF full‑band speech/audio codec (8–48 kHz, wide bitrate range) used in WebRTC; supports NB→FB, low delay, VBR/CBR.
3GPP Enhanced Voice Services for VoLTE/5G, supporting NB/WB/SWB/FB with high robustness and quality.
Skype/3rd‑party ultra‑wideband speech codec (basis for Opus’ speech layer) optimized for conversational voice.
Internet Speech Audio Codec (wideband) used in WebRTC for low‑delay, adaptive bitrate speech.
